_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average price index of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice benchmarked to 2015 at 100, now stands at 132, reflecting a 32% increase over the period. This rise has been uneven and more pronounced in recent years. The index aggregates global commodity prices sourced from FRED and IMF data, providing a snapshot of key soft commodity trends affecting consumers. Not all components have contributed equally to this climb, indicating a varied price performance across items.
notes.movers: Coffee is the dominant driver with a 93% price increase since 2015, substantially outperforming the others. Orange juice prices are up 22%, while wheat and sugar have seen more modest rises of 7% and 5% respectively. These price shifts reflect specific weather events and crop diseases—such as frost, drought, and citrus greening—influencing supply and thus prices. These markets are relatively thin, meaning small changes in supply or demand can cause outsized price moves, unlike broader inflation trends.
notes.why: The headline increase in the breakfast basket is largely shaped by a few crops vulnerable to weather and disease conditions. Because these are specialized, weather-exposed commodities, price levels have the potential to remain elevated and volatile over multiple years. Understanding these dynamics helps contextualize commodity price movements beyond general inflation narratives.
